summary: Convert a vector data cube into a raster data cube
description:
Converts a vector data cube into a raster data cube (also known as "rasterize"). The spatial dimensions `x` and `y` of the raster data cube, i.e. their extent, resolution, reference system and labels, are taken from `target`. All other dimensions of `target` are ignored. The geometries are reprojected to the spatial reference system of `target` if needed.

The geometry dimension of `data` is replaced by the spatial dimensions `x` and `y`. All other dimensions of `data` remain unchanged, e.g. a dimension with properties of the geometries (see ``load_geojson()``) or the temporal and bands dimensions of the result of ``aggregate_spatial()``. If `data` only consists of the geometry dimension and has no values, the value `1` is used for all geometries, e.g. to create a mask.

By default, the values of a geometry are assigned to the following pixels:

- Polygons: all pixels whose center lies within the polygon. Whether a pixel whose center lies exactly on the boundary is assigned is implementation-dependent.
- Lines: the pixels on the render path of the line (as computed by the Bresenham line algorithm).
- Points: the pixel that contains the point.

If `all_touched` is `true`, all pixels that are touched by a geometry are assigned instead.

If multiple geometries are assigned to a pixel, which of their values are used is implementation-dependent. Pixels without a geometry are set to no-data.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: A raster data cube that defines the spatial dimensions `x` and `y` of the result. All other dimensions are ignored.

parameters.name: all_touched
parameters.description: If set to `true`, all pixels that are touched by a geometry are assigned the values of the geometry. Otherwise, only the pixels whose center lies within a polygon, the pixels on the render path of a line and the pixels that contain a point are assigned.

returns.description: A raster data cube with the spatial dimensions `x` and `y` of `target` and all dimensions of `data` except for the geometry dimension.
